# YM04: 镂月开云 Louyue Kaiyun, "Engraved Moon and Open Clouds"

Malone calls it The Peony Terrace.

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM04` · Page: `/scenes/#YM04` · Row: `research/buildings/YM04-louyue-kaiyun/`

## What it was

镂月开云 Louyue Kaiyun, first called 牡丹台 Mudan Tai, the Peony Terrace, stood behind 富春楼 Fuchun Lou on the east side of the Back Lake; its main hall is 纪恩堂 Ji'en Tang, with 御兰芬 Yulanfen to the north (S05 j80:26a). The old name was replaced in 1744 and the plaque 纪恩堂 was hung in 1766 (乾隆三十一年), with an essay recalling that here Yongzheng, then a prince, presented the young Hongli to the Kangxi Emperor at a peony viewing, after which Kangxi took him into the palace (S05 j80:26b-28b). Burned in October 1860 with the rest of the garden by British troops on Elgin's order (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **built** 雍正初 牡丹台 (S06); by 1722: named 牡丹臺 in a prince's poem (雍邸集); **changed** Renamed 1744 [j80:26b]; 纪恩堂 plaque 1766 [j80:26b-27a]; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S06, S01, S200).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Preface of 1744: "殿以香楠為材覆二色瓦煥若金碧前植牡丹數百本後列古松青青" (S05 j80:30a). The hall was built of fragrant nanmu and roofed with tiles of two colours, shining like gold and jade; several hundred peonies grew in front and old pines behind. A note in the poem says the peonies peak in the fourth month, when the capital is usually praying for rain, so in seven years of residence he had feasted at the blossom only once (S05 j80:30a-b; same theme in the 1746 poem E1196, S360).

### How later sources differ

S05 (1774+) names only 纪恩堂 and 御兰芬; the 1766 and 1767 poems add 养素书屋 Yangsu Shuwu beside 御兰芬, and a 1767 poem says the orchid hall 御兰芬 stood directly behind the peony terrace ("偶臨蘭蕙畹前即牡丹臺", E1198-E1200, S360). On the base plan S01 the main hall carries a label read only as "?云楼", not 纪恩堂, and the pavilion 来青亭 Laiqing Ting (YM04-N01) appears, which S05 does not name: so the plan state differs from the 1774 text at least in naming. No dated Jiaqing-Xianfeng rebuild was found in this pass.

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Nothing written yet.

### The garden around it

Peonies in hundreds in front of the hall, old pines behind, mixed flowering plants all round (S05 j80:30a); orchids at 御兰芬 beside white rocks, a clear spring, pine and bamboo (E1197, S360 1766 poem: "白石清泉側蒼松翠竹倫"). Roof of two-colour glazed tiles is the one stated colour scheme (S05 j80:30a); which two colours is not said.

## Gaps and wishlist

The leaf P0004 shows the front hall with a green-glazed roof edged in dark blue, which is probably the 二色瓦 'two-colour tiles' of the preface (my reading of the painting, C); the bays of 纪恩堂 (plan 9 cells by 2, which may include galleries); whether the plan label "?云楼" is a misreading of 镂月开云 or a later name.

### Open questions that name it
